issues.legal_issue: The requirement for periodic revision of municipal valuations and assessments is directory, and omission of a holding for good reason does not cause its existing assessment to lapse.
material_facts: A holding had an existing valuation and assessment that had been upheld in earlier proceedings.
The holding was omitted from a general revision of municipal assessments, and the omission was found to be for a valid reason.
The municipality sought to recover taxes on the basis of the existing assessment.
issues.conclusion: The existing valuation and assessment did not lapse merely because the holding was excluded from the general revision; they remained in force until altered or amended under the statutory procedure and a new list took effect.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 102 and 106 of the Bihar and Orissa Municipality Act, 1922, Section 106’s use of “ordinarily” qualifies the direction to prepare new valuation and assessment lists every five years. Revision and inclusion of every holding are therefore directory, permitting omission in extraordinary circumstances or for good reason. Under Section 106(2), an existing valuation or assessment remains valid until a new list takes effect; Sections 105 and 107 provide for preparation and alteration or amendment of assessment lists. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.municipal_tax_recovery_proceeding: A municipality brought a proceeding to recover taxes assessed on a holding.
predicates.holding_omitted_for_good_reason: The holding was left out of a general assessment revision for a good reason.
predicates.prior_assessment_in_force: A valuation or assessment for the holding was in force before the general revision.

issues.definition: When a municipality seeks to recover taxes, a holding is omitted from a general revision for good reason, and its prior assessment is in force, that assessment remains in force until replaced.

issues.legal_issue: A mixed question of law and fact raised for the first time on appeal is not entertained when the opposing party had no opportunity to present evidence on it.
material_facts: The objection concerning the procedure for increasing the assessment was not raised in the written statement or before the lower courts.
No issue was framed on that objection, and it was not argued before the High Court.
The objection involved both law and fact, and the municipality had no opportunity to lead evidence concerning compliance with the relevant requirements.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused to entertain the objection when raised for the first time in the appeal, while noting that it could be raised properly in proceedings concerning later tax periods.
issues.legal_principle: A mixed question of law and fact cannot be raised for the first time on appeal where the opposing party had no opportunity to lead evidence on it. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: civil_appeal and plea_not_raised_below and plea_mixed_law_and_fact and opponent_lacked_opportunity_to_present_evidence

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal.
predicates.plea_not_raised_below: The party raising the plea did not raise it in the proceedings before the lower courts.
predicates.plea_mixed_law_and_fact: The plea depends on both legal and factual matters.
predicates.opponent_lacked_opportunity_to_present_e: The opposing party had no opportunity in the lower proceedings to present evidence relevant to the plea.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, a plea not raised below that involves both law and fact is not entertained when the opposing party lacked an opportunity to present evidence on it.
